metadata.scope: A design pass on all 16 enrolled lessons across Volumes I–IV, not a rollout to every image.
metadata.implementation_limit: These 16 storyboards are proposals. The separate quantization prototype now uses focused number-line and retained-register scenes; no production players changed.
metadata.learner_evidence: Design/source review only. No actual student feedback, user study, preference ranking, or measured learning gain is asserted.
metadata.artwork_review: Rendered the 16 current canonical source assets from the existing HTML build and inspected contact sheets. Read local source/context and runtime JS/CSS. Did not rerender all interactive states or rebuild print targets for this design pass.

software.primary: Semantic HTML controls + inline SVG scene + scoped CSS + small browser JavaScript controller.
software.motion: Native Web Animations API or CSS transitions for interpolation. Keep stable objects/paths with declared causal transitions and one deterministic state reducer. Interpolation never owns numerical state.
software.why: SVG retains crisp labels and inspectable spatial identity; native browser controls fit Quarto and avoid a separate application or export pipeline.
software.avoid: Do not introduce React, a new bundler, CDN scripts, video/GIF as the primary player, or Canvas/WebGL without an actual rendering need.
software.formats: HTML animates; PDF/EPUB/print/no-JavaScript keep the canonical complete static asset. Reduced motion uses equivalent discrete states.

metadata.web_design_freedom: The source drawings provide context, not immutable geometry. The web may redraw, zoom, reflow, or replace a scene to teach the mechanism more clearly. Preserve mathematical meaning, object identity, logical dependencies, units, ownership, and stated scope; retain complete canonical static figures for print.
metadata.learner_iteration: Version2 underwent two simulated learner/design/technical review rounds. Real student feedback remains uncollected; learner-session.html is a blank local protocol.

static_selection_policy.default: Keep the other 691 figures static. No inactive tabs or player controls, no coverage quotas, and no revival of withdrawn guided tours.
gate: Name one transformation, spatial computation, causal handoff, allocation/release boundary, or ownership change that students can observe more clearly than in the complete static figure.

Preserve technical meaning, object identity, units, ownership, logical dependencies, and assumptions. Choose web geometry freely when it improves understanding; the canonical static figure remains complete. Numeric toys are explicitly supplementary.
Make before→transition→after visible in the same diagram. A moving border, glow, traveling unlabeled dot, or prose slideshow does not qualify.
Keep persistent state visible through the sequence; show copies versus moves and retained versus released resources when relevant.
Use only a short current-action sentence by default. Detailed arithmetic/ledger/schema appears on selecting the relevant object.
Verify the actual themed chapter, desktop/narrow, light/dark, pause/manual jumps, reduced motion, and static fallback before calling it integrated.
normally_static: D·A·M intersection landscape and other taxonomies
chapter maps and conceptual relationship overviews
static architecture inventories without a specific runtime mechanism
historical/observational plots without a justified inspection interaction
static_selection_policy.edge_cases: Tensor layout can remain an interactive lookup without continuous animation. Stopping-budget may revert to static if cumulative comparison adds no learner value. Stateful does not automatically mean animation-worthy.

lessons.title: Convolution Operation
lessons.review_basis: Read current controller, stylesheet, local figure source/context, and inspected rendered canonical artwork. This is a design/source review; it is not a new runtime or learner study.
lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review
lessons.revision_scope: medium: retain SVG grids and state data, reduce arithmetic prominence, add stable moving receptive field and write path
lessons.existing_strength: Current SVG preserves the perspective and grid sizes. It computes real products and output values, retains written outputs, and already has a movable window and connecting lines.
lessons.current_gap: A product worksheet competes with the spatial story. A changed window and completed number do not yet show a coherent contribution traveling from that window to its output.
storyboard: Show the input and fixed filter before movement; select an edge window with a nonzero result.
Move the orange window across one column while the same filter remains visible; keep overlapping input cells recognizable.
Briefly show the nine selected values contributing through the existing blue connection to one persistent output cell; update its running contribution locally.
Write the completed output once; leave it visible while the window advances to the next position.
Complete one row, then offer the remaining scan at a faster illustrative pace.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: Filter values stay unchanged across positions; completed output cells remain stored. A logical read highlight is not a claim of a DRAM fetch.
lessons.optional_calculation: Open the current output cell to inspect its nine products and partial sum. Keep the formula adjacent to that cell; default view emphasizes window-to-output correspondence.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: Declare single-channel, valid, stride-one cross-correlation. Do not imply channel reductions, cache misses, parallel scheduling, or measured execution speed.
lessons.source_visual_context: Retain the original perspective: dashed 7×7 input below, orange 3×3 receptive field, violet 5×5 output above, and blue connections between the active window and one output cell.

lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review
lessons.decision: keep as interactive mapping; motion only for a trace
lessons.revision_scope: medium: stable routing overlay above the existing grids; optional traversal playback
lessons.existing_strength: Cell selection and both mappings are correct; original six values, stride conventions, and simultaneous layouts are preserved.
lessons.current_gap: Controller explicitly uses no movement. Selecting and highlighting destinations can remain useful, but advancing a five-step explanation is not itself a mechanism animation.
storyboard: Select value 5 at tensor[1,1]; keep its source cell visible.
Trace an address-lookup marker from the cell to row-major offset 4 and column-major offset 3; both storage arrays remain unchanged.
Choose a row-wise traversal and move a read cursor through tensor cells 1,2,3,4,5,6 while a linked cursor visits corresponding offsets in each array.
Leave a subtle numbered trail showing contiguous accesses versus jumps; stop with both complete routes visible.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: These are two alternative layouts, not two buffers being copied during selection. Storage contents stay fixed; cursors represent references/reads.
lessons.optional_calculation: Selecting a destination reveals i×stride[0]+j×stride[1], then offset×element_bytes, with units explicit.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: Do not animate cells flying out of one tensor into both arrays: that would suggest copying or physical reordering. Do not claim measured cache performance from six-element traversal.
lessons.source_visual_context: Keep the 2×3 blue tensor on the left and the pink row-major and green column-major arrays stacked on the right; keep original values and zero-based offsets.

lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review

lessons.existing_strength: The deterministic schedule correctly retains intermediates until their final consumer and exposes saved versus recomputed values.
lessons.current_gap: Node classes and lifetime labels jump between states. The learner must read narration to infer which activation produced the next one and why a value remains live.
storyboard: A labeled activation advances through the forward chain; a0 and a3 acquire persistent saved-state badges.
After the forward consumer finishes, a1 and a2 become dashed; the saved checkpoints remain filled.
At backward layer 4, trace a replay from a3 to reconstruct a4 in orange, then show its backward consumer.
Replay from a0 through a1 and a2; keep both orange nodes filled while backward consumes the segment in reverse.
Remove each live badge only after its last backward consumer; leave the saved/recomputed history legible.

lessons.misinterpretation_guard: Playback seconds are reading time. The five illustrated activations exclude gradients, weights, optimizer state, loss state, and workspaces.

lessons.title: Quantized Matrix Multiplication Pipeline
lessons.review_basis: Read current controller, stylesheet, local figure source/context, and inspected rendered canonical artwork. This is a design/source review; it is not a new runtime or learner study.
lessons.status: working review prototype; production player unchanged
lessons.revision_scope: large presentation change: replace dashboard-first layout with the original pipeline and optional arithmetic; retain checked numeric state
lessons.existing_strength: Both declared scales have verified rounding, zero-point correction, accumulation, output reconstruction, and unchanged six-byte operand storage.
lessons.current_gap: The implementation is a worked-calculation dashboard. Cards, repeating labels, and comparison tables displace the original connected pipeline, forcing the reader to assemble dataflow mentally.
storyboard: Retain indexed FP32 input cards and read one value onto a real-number line.
Snap the marker to the nearest representable real level; retain the original marker and show the corresponding stored INT8 code separately.
Preserve indexed code arrays while zero-point-corrected operands form a product.
Move that product into the retained register; show old sum + arrived product, then the new sum.
Interpret the wide sum in real units before rounding onto the output grid; show connected ReLU passage and final code/reconstruction.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: Operand sources remain in place when read; moving glyphs represent logical contributions, not destructive moves. The red INT32 register retains the partial sum until every pair contributes.
lessons.optional_calculation: Selecting a block opens just its current transformation: q=round(x/s)+z, centered product, accumulator update, or output requantization. Detailed comparison is secondary and optional.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: The worked case is 1×3 by 3×1 with declared scales/zero-points. Keep requantization before activation as in the figure. Logical flow is not a literal per-scalar Tensor Core execution trace or hardware timing.
lessons.source_visual_context: Keep the two floating-input branches on the left, violet quantizers, blue multiplication at their convergence, red INT32 output, then green requantization, activation, and final INT8 output in their original left-to-right order.

lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review

lessons.revision_scope: medium: overlay explicit copy routes and local residency without replacing matrix geometry
lessons.existing_strength: The current example separates backing memory from on-chip copies, retains partial C across K tiles, and performs one final write.
lessons.current_gap: Values appear in separate on-chip cards without a visual copy path from their source tiles; the learner must connect matrices, copies, and accumulation through prose.
storyboard: Select the blue C tile; initialize its on-chip accumulator to zero while its backing-memory destination remains unwritten.
Move labeled copies of the active green A and pink B tiles into the fast-storage inset; source tiles remain visible.
Show the resident operand tiles contributing to the blue accumulator and updating its partial values.
Advance K and replace only operand copies; keep the same accumulator object and its previous values visible.
Send the completed C tile to its backing-memory destination once; then mark local storage reusable.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: A/B transfers are copies; source data is retained. C partial sums remain on chip across K blocks. Release local storage after the final write.
lessons.optional_calculation: Select one accumulator cell to inspect 0+9×1+10×3=39, then 39+11×5+12×7=178. Keep traffic counts in an optional details layer.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: The explicit 4×4 / 4×6 toy schedule counts logical scalar copies and MACs, not measured DRAM transactions or achieved throughput.

lessons.title: Two-phase checkpoint staging

lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review
lessons.decision: keep; make two copies and commit boundary tangible
lessons.revision_scope: medium: stable timeline with named shard tokens and restore-point pointer
lessons.existing_strength: Current state distinguishes resume at t1 from commit at t3 and correctly retains the immutable local snapshot while training advances.
lessons.current_gap: Timeline boxes change classes; no named shard visibly travels between locations. Resume, persistence, and publication are explained largely in text and a separate table.
storyboard: At t0, pause the training lane and copy generation g into a labeled local NVMe shard; retain the prior committed generation marker.
At t1, unfreeze training while generation g stays fixed in NVMe.
Show a copy of shard g traveling to parallel FS under continuing training; retain the local source until its consumer completes.
Collect all required shard/checksum confirmations at the coordinator; restore still points to generation g−1.
Publish manifest g last; only then move the restore-point marker to g. Local staging can subsequently become reusable.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: Separate changing live training state, immutable local snapshot, durable shard copies, and committed manifest. A copied shard alone does not change the restore point.
lessons.optional_calculation: Optional generation/location table and t0–t3 interval explanation; do not introduce throughput values absent from the chapter.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: Animate logical copies and dependency order. Lane widths are schematic; no proportional speedup or implied zero bandwidth cost.
lessons.source_visual_context: Retain four lanes—training, local NVMe, parallel FS, coordinator—and t0–t3 positions, with staged/not-restorable and restorable brackets.

lessons.title: Hierarchical AllReduce
lessons.review_basis: Read current controller, stylesheet, local figure source/context, and inspected rendered canonical artwork. This is a design/source review; it is not a new runtime or learner study.
lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review
lessons.decision: keep; move named shards across original links
lessons.revision_scope: medium-large: stable GPU/shard SVG scene with persistent object identity across three phases
lessons.existing_strength: Current controller distinguishes node partial sums, global sums, and final local copies; it avoids double reduction during AllGather.
lessons.current_gap: Cards replace symbolic contents and highlight links; actual shard transfer and combination are not shown. Three snapshots can be mistaken for three separate systems.
storyboard: Introduce per-rank A/B contributions in the first panel; explicitly label the three panels as successive views of the same ranks.
Trace the two local contributions to the GPU retaining each node-shard partial sum; unowned shard slots become empty after ReduceScatter.
Send matching A and B partials along their corresponding inter-node links in the middle panel; combine them into ΣA and ΣB.
Copy each global shard across local NVLink in the last panel, leaving its original owner intact.
Stop when each rank visibly holds the same [ΣA,ΣB] result.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: ReduceScatter partitions ownership; shard AllReduce produces global values; AllGather duplicates existing global results instead of summing again.
lessons.optional_calculation: Optional symbolic reduction identities or one small numeric shard example, never required to follow which shard travels where.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: The schematic has two representative ranks per node. Link animation duration does not encode NVLink/InfiniBand bandwidth or a complete concrete collective algorithm.
lessons.source_visual_context: Retain three phase panels, two nodes per panel, two GPUs per node, horizontal NVLink bars, vertical corresponding-GPU InfiniBand links, and partial/full-shard legend.

lessons.title: Communication-computation overlap

lessons.revision_scope: medium: stable timeline geometry and linked dependency markers; reduce table prominence
lessons.existing_strength: Current discrete states account for nonoverlappable overhead, concurrent compute/transfer, and the final gradient dependency.
lessons.current_gap: The timeline changes box states but the causal handoff from completed local gradient to launched collective is not visually explicit.
storyboard: Advance one shared schematic cursor through backward L4; mark its local gradient ready at block end.
During the amber o slice keep the GPU occupied, then route the ready-gradient marker into AllReduce L4.
Continue the same cursor through backward L3 while its network counterpart advances through AllReduce L4; show both active together.
Repeat handoffs until L1; retain completed-gradient marks.
At the exposed tail, stop GPU work while L1 communication finishes; only then open the optimizer dependency gate.

lessons.misinterpretation_guard: Keep the source assumption that each earlier transfer fits beneath the next backward block. Slower transfers may expose more waiting; do not universalize this schedule.

lessons.title: KV cache fragmentation and the PagedAttention solution

lessons.revision_scope: medium: stable slots/table with traced allocation and final-reader retention
lessons.existing_strength: Current mapping [0,1,4,5], selectable lookup, final-page slack, capacity accounting, and last-reader release are explicit and correct.
lessons.current_gap: Rows/cells change text and highlights with no routed logical-page-to-physical-slot trace. Extra prose and quizzes compete with the allocation story.
storyboard: Briefly show reserved-unused slots in (a) and the two separate gaps in (b), without morphing A/B into C/D.
In panel (c), allocate E0 into physical slot0 and write table[0]=0; retain C/D where they are.
Allocate E1→1, E2→4, E3→5; animate each table-mediated lookup route rather than moving existing C/D pages.
Choose logical page2 and trace table[2]→slot4; keep indices visible at every hop.
Stop E generation but leave its pages filled while a final-reader marker remains active; release table entries and slots only after that reader completes.

lessons.title: Block Table Indirection and Tail Copy-on-Write

lessons.revision_scope: large presentation change: restore original arrows and shared physical objects instead of repeated card lists
lessons.existing_strength: Current state separates allocated-unwritten, free, initialized, and other-request storage. It copies the two valid tail entries before committing B’s table change.
lessons.current_gap: The current card/grid reconstruction omits the source arrow geometry and repeats blocks in different card groups. This weakens physical identity and shared ownership—the central lesson.
storyboard: Trace token9 from logical block2 through table entry9 to physical block9, slot1, along the original elbow path.
Fork candidate B by adding a second reference to the same physical blocks3,7,9; do not create duplicate physical blocks.
Allocate private block14 for B while its active tail reference still points to9.
Copy initialized entries8 and9 from physical9 slots0–1 into physical14 slots0–1; retain A’s unchanged source.
Commit B table[2]=14 only after the copy; append token10 in block14 slot2. Leave full blocks3 and7 jointly referenced.

lessons.title: One operation, many attempts
lessons.review_basis: Read current controller, stylesheet, local figure source/context, and inspected rendered canonical artwork. This is a design/source review; it is not a new runtime or learner study.
lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review
lessons.decision: keep; animate one identity across retries and one selected branch
lessons.revision_scope: large presentation change: stable original runtime/endpoint flow with traveling request/reply glyphs
lessons.existing_strength: Current branch selector correctly treats completed/running/conflict/fresh as alternatives and preserves the operation identifier and scoped contract.
lessons.current_gap: The current scene mostly consists of explanatory cards. Timeout mentions another attempt, but does not visibly send a retry with the same operation ID and a different attempt ID.
storyboard: Create op-42 once at admission; display attempt-1 as a separate envelope carrying op-42 and its bound payload.
Send that envelope to the endpoint lookup; route it through only the selected branch.
In the fresh case, commit effect and result together inside the supported transaction boundary.
If the reply is lost, retain the endpoint result but show runtime outcome unknown; send attempt-2 carrying the same op-42.
Route the retry to completed→retained result; return the reply without firing a second effect. Offer running/conflict as separate cases.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: Operation identity, bound payload, retained endpoint record, caller/resource scope, and retention window persist independently of transient attempts and runtime uncertainty.
lessons.optional_calculation: Optional request envelope fields and count of new committed effects; no artificial arithmetic needed.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: Timeout does not prove nonexecution. Exactly-once behavior is conditional on endpoint deduplication and supported atomicity; the motion must not promise universal exactly-once external effects.
lessons.source_visual_context: Retain runtime column on left, endpoint lookup on right, timeout retry loop, four distinct lookup branches, no-new-effect bracket, and apply-effect/record-result transaction boundary.

lessons.title: Intent Before Dispatch
lessons.review_basis: Read current controller, stylesheet, local figure source/context, and inspected rendered canonical artwork. This is a design/source review; it is not a new runtime or learner study.
lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review
lessons.decision: keep; show the durability gate and knowledge state separately
lessons.revision_scope: large presentation change: reestablish the original event row, barrier line, and recovery bands
lessons.existing_strength: Current alternative cases distinguish lost acknowledgment, crash after acknowledgment, and timeout; recovery remains in doubt without adequate correlated evidence.
lessons.current_gap: The barrier is rendered as an explanatory card rather than a spatial gate. Persistent event ordering and recovery knowledge are hard to connect visually.
storyboard: Move a proposal marker to admission and show reservation; the dispatch arrow remains blocked.
Write the intent under the declared failure domain and wait for its acknowledgment; optionally lose that acknowledgment while the durable record remains.
Only after acknowledgment open the dispatch gate and move the request outward.
Pause or crash at the chosen boundary; align a vertical marker with the recovery band below, keeping unknown outcome visually distinct from request location.
Move correlated evidence into the recorded-evidence event; only then change the recovery band to established.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: Reservation, durable intent, acknowledgment receipt, in-flight request, and recorded evidence are separate state. Runtime knowledge can lag the external effect.
lessons.optional_calculation: Optional event log and authoritative-prefix explanation; no numerical worked case is necessary.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: An acknowledged intent does not prove dispatch or an external effect. Crash after acknowledgment but before dispatch can remain in doubt during recovery; absent intent proves non-dispatch only with a complete authoritative prefix.
lessons.source_visual_context: Keep proposal→admission→intent acknowledgment→dispatch→evidence row; the durability barrier separates acknowledgment and dispatch. Preserve recovery bands below.

lessons.title: Conservation Across a Canceled Child

On trace closure, transfer its settled part into root settled and return only its unused part to root free.
At fuzzing local stop, expand its reserved segment into the child account; leave the root reservation visibly unchanged.

lessons.title: One range return updates only the cells it touched

lessons.review_basis: Read current controller, stylesheet, local figure source/context, and inspected rendered canonical artwork. This is a design/source review; it is not a new runtime or learner study.
lessons.status: planned; no production lesson changed by this review
lessons.decision: borderline; static chart first, optional cumulative comparison rather than a token-flow player
lessons.revision_scope: reconsider enrollment after prototype feedback; small optional chart interaction, no new vehicle simulation
lessons.existing_strength: Current state already derives the additive terms and separately charges dispatch-to-admission travel; it avoids calling the preliminary gap a net reserve.
lessons.current_gap: Growing one more bar can simply repeat the table and prose. This figure has no natural moving value path, and forcing one would distract from a precise conditional accounting argument.
storyboard: Default to the complete static chart, readable without playback.
Optional compare control reveals a subtotal’s constituent segments beside the clearance line; earlier contributions stay visible.
Selecting the jerk/tracking terms shows exactly which added distances cross clearance, preserving the same scale.
Compare the candidate-speed bar using the same terms; charge dispatch-to-admission before labeling the remaining reserve.
If this adds no understanding in learner review, remove Explore for this figure and keep the chart static.
lessons.retained_memory_or_ownership: These are conservative distance contributions, not memory ownership. Keep one consistent clearance reference and avoid counting a subtotal as available safe margin.
lessons.optional_calculation: Optional selected-term formula and source-table rows; no extra math dashboard or animated vehicle needed.
lessons.misinterpretation_guard: Do not treat the stack as a literal temporal braking trajectory: braking, age, margins, and tracking terms are not all successive physical motion intervals. Assumptions about load/floor/speed remain explicit.
lessons.source_visual_context: Preserve the source stacked bars, millimeter axis, seven drive-limit cumulative bars, eighth aisle-speed bar, clearance line, and exact source-table terms.
